Fine-tuning

You might say

Support replies keep changing tone and format. Should we train a model?

Continuing to train an existing model with task examples so its outputs better match them on a specific task·A support team wants every refund reply to state the outcome before the next step. Fine-tuning can continue training a model with representative inputs and target replies; compare it on tickets not used for training to see whether it helps, and still provide the current task instructions.
Know first
Prompt
Fine tuning
What does fine-tuning change in a support task?
Support · refund question
Support ticket · teaching exampleGoal: outcome first, next step second
Customer messageThe cup is unopened. Can I return it?
Current replyFind the return option on the order page. Unused products can be returned.

Teaching example: the team names a concrete difference—the reply should state the outcome before the next step.

How to tell whether fine-tuning helped

Examples show the target behavior: Representative inputs and target outputs provide examples for further training. There is no single sample count that fits every model and task.

Evaluate on new inputs: Training examples do not prove that new requests will work. Keep tickets outside the training set and compare correctness, format, and tone.

Fine-tuning does not remove prompts or guarantee correctness

It makes outputs better match training examples; it does not guarantee every new answer follows them or knows current policy. Use an updatable source for changing information.
